title: Why Do We Get HICCUPS? 🫢
description:
You chug a soda on a first date... and HIC. Smooth.

A hiccup is your breathing muscle, the diaphragm, jerking all of a sudden. Air rushes in, and a split second later your vocal cords snap shut on it: that is the "hic". A stomach swollen with fizz, a big meal or swallowed air is the usual trigger, because it sits right under that muscle. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Why do we have the reflex at all? Nobody knows for sure. One idea, still unproven: it is left over from our amphibian ancestors. Tadpoles pump water over their gills with the door to their lungs shut, a move that looks a lot like a hiccup. Bonus fact: you were already hiccuping before you were born.
